Classes for a numeric characteristic, cut only between distinct values

Source: R/classes.R
screen_classes.Rd

screen_classes() turns a numeric characteristic into a factor of about k classes of roughly equal mass for shadow_screen(). Unlike quantile classes from cut() and quantile(), a class boundary never falls on a value that occurs in the data, so no observation depends on whether intervals are closed on the left or the right. That matters for characteristics with heaped values: loan amounts cluster on round numbers, and quantiles then land exactly on those heaps.

Usage

screen_classes(x, k = 10, support = range(x, na.rm = TRUE))

Arguments

x

A numeric vector. NA stays NA.

k

Target number of classes inside the support. Default 10.

support

Length-two range; values outside it get the classes "below" and "above". Default: the range of x, i.e. none.

Value

A factor, levels ordered from below to above, with attribute "heaping": the share of rows inside the support that lie on a value at which quantile()-based k-classes would place a boundary. Above a few percent, quantile classes would assign a material part of the sample by convention.

Details

Values outside support get classes of their own, "below" and "above". Pass as support the range of the characteristic among the rows whose outcome is observed: a lender that never accepts below a score cut-off then shows up as one class with no accepted row, which is the step that a linear term in the response model cannot represent. shadow_screen() does this itself with numeric = "classes".

Classes are built greedily from the smallest value up: a class is closed once it holds at least its share \(1/k\) of the rows inside the support. A single value holding more than that share forms a class of its own, so class masses vary; a last class smaller than half its share is merged into the one before. With at most k distinct values every value is its own class.

See also

shadow_screen()

Examples

amount <- c(rep(10000, 30), rep(5000, 20), round(runif(50, 1000, 35000), -2))
f <- screen_classes(amount, k = 5)
table(f)
#> f
#>   [1,300, 5,000]  [6,300, 10,000] [10,900, 24,100] [24,400, 34,700] 
#>               27               37               20               16 
attr(f, "heaping")
#> [1] 0.5
# a cut-off: nothing below 662 was ever accepted
score <- round(runif(200, 600, 800))
table(screen_classes(score, k = 4, support = c(662, 800)))
#> 
#>      below [663, 702] [704, 735] [736, 771] [772, 800] 
#>         56         37         36         37         34
